title: The Regiment of the Lower Danube
premise: In the winter of 1913, on the frost-bound banks of the Lower Danube, Beatrix Iversen serves as driver and letter-reader to the suffragist Countess Ilona Vay, memorizing which secrets must never be spoken. When an abandoned child arrives at the estate gate with a note demanding the face be forgotten, Beatrix recognizes the boy as the son of Stefan, a river smuggler who once saved his life and now stands accused of treason against the Empire. As war fever turns neighbor against neighbor, Beatrix must choose between the countess's cause, his own carefully constructed invisibility, and a peacetime promise to ferry the boy downriver to safety before the ice breaks. He succeeds at terrible cost: exposed as a former deserter, he loses his place in the household but gains a family, delivering the child to Stefan's sister across the border as the first spring barges pass.
about_author: Mara Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town correspondence from the Austro-Hungarian frontier. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of empire, and lives near a river that freezes every winter.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unopened Things
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Establishes his routine: driving the Countess through frozen market towns, reading her correspondence aloud, deciding which silences protect whom. A letter arrives bearing a customs seal he doesn't recognize. Emotional beat: the comfort of invisibility, and its first hairline crack.

chapters.title: A Child at the Gate
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At dawn, a boy of six stands at the servants' entrance with a note: 'Forget this face.' The handwriting is Stefan's—the smuggler who pulled Beatrix from the Danube five years ago. The Countess orders the child fed but asks no questions. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in tenderness; the past knocking literally at the door.

chapters.title: What the Countess Knows
chapters.summary: Countess Ilona's POV. She recognizes the boy's surname from intercepted police correspondence and realizes Beatrix is hiding something. She chooses not to press—yet—while weighing how a scandal could destroy the suffrage petition she's carrying to Vienna. Emotional beat: the loneliness of power and the arithmetic of mercy.

chapters.title: Letters That Burn
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He decodes a warning hidden in a laundry list: Stefan has been named in a treason inquiry and the gendarmes will sweep the river villages by month's end. Beatrix burns the list and lies to the Countess for the first time. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into resolve; the promise made in peacetime becomes a debt due now.

chapters.title: The Ice Road
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He scouts the frozen river with the boy, Milos, disguised as his nephew, mapping the crossing to the Serbian bank where Stefan's sister lives. An old ferryman recognizes Beatrix's face and says nothing—but saw it. Emotional beat: fragile hope; two fugitives learning each other's fears on the ice.

chapters.title: Enemy Declarations
chapters.summary: Countess Ilona's POV. War rumors harden; Serbian names become suspect overnight. A gendarme captain calls at the estate asking after 'a woman's servant seen on the ice.' Ilona covers for Beatrix, then demands the truth. Emotional beat: alliance forged under pressure, trust tested by state fear.

chapters.title: The Confession in the Coach House
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. He tells Ilona everything: the desertion five years ago, Stefan's rescue, the debt of silence. She reveals she knew of a deserter all along and shielded him because justice and law diverged long ago. They plan the crossing together for the night before the ice breaks. Emotional beat: relief and terror entwined; identity surrendered and reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Captain's Net
chapters.summary: Countess Ilona's POV. The captain returns with a warrant and traps Ilona into a lie she cannot sustain. Beatrix is detained in the coach house; Milos hides in the laundry cart. Ilona stalls with legal maneuvering while the river begins to groan and shift. Emotional beat: rising panic; institutions closing like a fist.

chapters.title: Before the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Escaping during a blackout drill, Beatrix takes the coach, the boy, and the last stable darkness toward the crossing. The ice cracks under the wheels mid-river; he carries Milos the final hundred meters as the surface fails behind them. On the far bank, the sister waits. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice, speed, and the promise kept at the edge of drowning.

chapters.title: The Regiment of the Lower Danube
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Beatrix surrenders himself rather than let Ilona hang for the lie; his desertion record surfaces, but so does Stefan's old testimony clearing him of treason. Pardoned but unemployable, he stays on as the Countess's gardener, watching spring barges carry letters he no longer needs to read. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—justice outside the law, inheritance chosen, a self no longer invisible.
